thread:
ashley_sales: Heads up — Acme POC on Dedicated is blocked. Several users report 'Invalid audience' during SSO. Using tenant acme-poc. Can SE look?

paul_se: Likely audience/entityID mismatch. What did they set in Okta for Entity ID and ACS?

ashley_sales: Okta app shows: Entity ID = https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai/saml/metadata
ACS = https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai/saml/acs

cheng_eng: Two quick things: 1) Audience in SAML must exactly match entityID (including path, no extra slash). 2) If SCIM created duplicate users, the user may be routed to wrong tenant mapping.

ashley_sales: Their SAML logs: "SAMLResponse validation failed: AudienceRestriction validation failed. expected https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai/saml/metadata but got https://redwood-inference.com"

sam_cs: Customer also sees occasional 403 after login. They refresh and sometimes can access, other times 403.

okta-bot: SCIM event: POST /Users -> 409 Conflict. payload: {"detail":"User already exists","status":"409"}

paul_se: 409 suggests Okta tried to create a user with an externalId we already have. If Okta provisioning is set to create+update, it can conflict. Recommend switching to 'create only' or 'update existing' while we reconcile.

cheng_eng: For SAML, ask them to decode the SAMLResponse and paste the <Audience> value only. Example snippet: <saml:Audience>https://redwood-inference.com</saml:Audience>

ashley_sales: Requested decoded assertion and SCIM failure body from Acme. Also flagged that they attempted to test with Hosted API key — reminded them Dedicated uses separate keys/endpoints.

paul_se: If they share raw base64 SAMLResponse I can decode and run validation locally. Also ask for exported Okta app settings JSON.

cheng_eng: Quick checklist: - Confirm Okta Entity ID == tenant entityID exactly. - Confirm ACS URL matches. - Confirm NameID format (email). - For SCIM, inspect response for existing externalId and map to our user ID.

sam_cs: I'll coordinate with their IAM admin to get assertion and SCIM payloads. They said group provisioning had intermittent 201/409 mix.

okta-bot: SCIM event: PATCH /Groups/acme-poc -> 200 OK

paul_se: FYI duplicates can cause routing to pick wrong org record which changes expected audience in assertion -> invalid audience. We can also paste a validation tool snippet for them.

ashley_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up once Acme sends the decoded assertion and the SCIM 409 body. :thumbsup:
